intro: Taking a position, conceding a point, disagreeing politely and holding your turn in a discussion.
p.a favor de.consejo: You say «estar a favor de» something or «a favor de que» + subjunctive: «a favor de que vengas».
p.en contra de.consejo: The opposite of «a favor de». With a conjugated verb: «en contra de que» + subjunctive.
p.punto de vista.consejo: You say «desde mi punto de vista» to give an opinion. The indicative follows.
p.a mi modo de ver.consejo: It opens a personal opinion. It is a little more formal than «yo creo que».
p.no cabe duda.consejo: You say «no cabe duda de que» + indicative, because it presents something as certain.
p.tener en cuenta.consejo: You say «hay que tener en cuenta que» + indicative. The «cuenta» is not the bank kind.
p.es cierto que.consejo: It recognises a point before answering: «Es cierto que…, pero…». It takes the indicative.
p.hasta cierto punto.consejo: It is used to agree only partly. The c of «cierto» sounds th: «THYER-to».
p.déjame terminar.consejo: It is firm but polite. «Déjame» has a tilde because it is proparoxytone: «DE-ha-me».
p.perdona que te interrumpa.consejo: After «perdona que» comes the subjunctive: «interrumpa». It is a polite way of asking for a turn.
p.hace falta.consejo: You say «hace falta algo» or «hace falta + infinitive». The thing needed is the subject.
p.opinión.consejo: You say «dar la opinión» and «cambiar de opinión». It ends in «-ión», like «decisión».
b1.titulo: Holding your own in a debate
b1.texto:
**Your position**: estoy **a favor de** / **en contra de** + noun or infinitive, or + **que** + subjunctive. Estoy en contra de que **cambien** el horario de la clase.

**Your opinion**, affirmative, takes the indicative: **desde mi punto de vista**, **a mi modo de ver**, **considero que**, **no cabe duda de que**. In the negative it takes the subjunctive: **no creo que**, **no me parece que**, **dudo que**.

**Concede, then answer**: **es cierto que**… **pero**…; **puede que tengas razón, pero**…; **hasta cierto punto**.

**Disagree politely**: **no comparto tu opinión**; **no estoy del todo de acuerdo**; **yo no lo veo así**.

**Manage the turns**: **perdona que te interrumpa**; **déjame terminar**; **como iba diciendo**; **¿puedo añadir algo?**

**Close**: **en resumen**, **lo que quiero decir es que**…
b2.f0.texto: I am in favour of us adopting a dog.
b2.f1.texto: We have to bear in mind that the flat is very small.
b2.f2.texto: There is no doubt that a dog gives a lot of company.
b2.f3.texto: I do not think it is the best pet for us.
b2.f6.texto: The way I see it, first we need more space.
b4.titulo: Indicative or subjunctive when giving opinions
b4.texto:
The mood of the second verb depends on whether you present something as **certain** or not.

- **Certainty** → indicative: **no cabe duda de que** la sopa **está** rica; **desde mi punto de vista**, **es** una buena idea.
- **Doubt or rejection** → subjunctive: **no creo que** sea buena idea; **dudo que** llegue.
- **Position with «que»** → subjunctive: estoy **en contra de que** cambien el horario; estoy **a favor de que** adoptemos un perro.
- **Same subject** → infinitive: estoy a favor de **adoptar** un perro.

**Acknowledging an idea before answering**: **es cierto que** el piso es pequeño, **pero**…
b4.e0.texto: I am against them changing the timetable.
b4.e1.texto: There is no doubt that the soup is very tasty.
b4.e2.texto: I do not think it is the best idea.
b5.f0.texto: The terrace smells of lemon and freshly made coffee.
b5.f1.texto: Two neighbours sit face to face with their hands on the table.
b5.f2.texto: One defends his idea with a calm, firm voice.
b5.f3.texto: The other listens with a frown and nods now and then.
b5.f4.texto: Between them, a jug of water sweats cold drops onto the tablecloth.
b5.f5.texto: The afternoon sun draws long shadows on the floor of the terrace.
b5.f6.texto: The words rise and fall like the leaves of the lemon tree.
b5.f7.texto: A bee buzzes for a moment over the jug and moves away.
b5.f8.texto: Little by little, the two neighbours lower the tone of their voices.
b5.f9.texto: In the end, a tired smile closes the discussion without winners.
b6.frase: Estoy en contra de que ____ el horario.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done: after «en contra de que» comes the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is indicative. Here the subjunctive is needed.
b6.pregunta: Complete: I am against them changing the timetable.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is it: «hasta cierto punto» means «partly».
b7.pregunta: You agree only in part. What do you say?
b8.frase: No cabe duda de que la sopa ____ muy rica.
b8.o0.refuerzo: A certainty takes the indicative, not the subjunctive.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That is it: «no cabe duda de que» states a fact.
b8.o2.refuerzo: After «la sopa» a conjugated verb is needed.
b8.pregunta: Complete: there is no doubt that the soup is tasty.
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is what the person interrupting says.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That is it: you politely ask to finish.
b9.pregunta: Someone cuts in while you are speaking. What do you say?
b10.frase: No creo que ____ la mejor idea.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Well done: a negative opinion takes the subjunctive.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Es» is indicative; «no creo que» asks for the subjunctive.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Será» is future; here the present subjunctive is needed.
b10.pregunta: Complete: I do not think it is the best idea.
b11.frase: Desde mi punto de vista hace falta más espacio
b11.traduccion: From my point of view we need more space
b12.pregunta: Write the opposite of «a favor de».
p.adoptemos.consejo: From «adoptar», to adopt. The «-emos» ending is for «nosotros» in the subjunctive.
p.espacio.consejo: The «c» before «i» is «th» in Spain. The stress falls on the middle syllable, «PA».
p.cambien.consejo: From «cambiar», to change. The «ie» diphthong is pronounced «byen».
p.defiende.consejo: From «defender», to defend. The «ie» forms a diphthong, pronounced «fyen».
p.asiente.consejo: From «asentir», to agree or nod. The stress falls on the diphthong «SYEN».
p.ratos.consejo: «A ratos» means now and then, from time to time. It is common in everyday talk.
p.suda.consejo: From «sudor», sweat. Here a jug «sweats» drops of cold water on its side.
p.limonero.consejo: From «limón», lemon, plus «-ero», the tree that bears it. The stress falls on «NE».
p.abeja.consejo: The «j» sounds like «h», and the «b» and «v» sound alike. The stress is on «BE».
p.tono.consejo: Here it means the tone of the voice, the level of loudness or kindness.
p.discusión.consejo: From «discutir», to discuss. The ending «-sión» is spelled with a tilde on the «ó».
p.vencedores.consejo: Plural of «vencedor». The «v» sounds like «b» and the «c» before «e» like «th».
